W
eighing in at a single ounce, the white-crowned sparrow can fly 2,600 miles, from Mexico to Alaska, on its annual spring migration, sometimes traveling 300 miles in a single night. Arctic terns make even longer journeys of 10,000 miles and more from the Arctic Circle to Antarctica, while great snipes fly over food-poor deserts and seas, sometimes covering 4,200 miles in four days without stopping.
During migration season, many bird species become continent-spanning, high-endurance athletes. “They’re flapping their wings several times a second for up to eight hours at a time,” said
Soren Coulson
, who studies migration physiology at the University of Memphis. For humans, an equivalent feat — say, running nonstop without food, water or rest for days at a time — would be unimaginable.
“We were just amazed and interested in how can these birds fly for thousands of miles without stopping, at a really high intensity, when most of us can barely run a 5K,” said
Paulo Mesquita
, who studies mitochondrial physiology and muscle aging at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation.
Scientists have long been fascinated with the
physiological changes
that birds undergo before and during migration. Some birds eat so much fat before their journeys that they double in body weight. In some species, their hearts are enlarged to pump more blood, or their digestive tracts grow and then shrink. But researchers have only recently started to explore at a fundamental level how migratory birds get the energy required to keep themselves aloft for days on end without eating.
Last year, two independent groups published research that explored migratory bird physiology in the lab and field to probe what happens at the subcellular level that allows birds to cover vast distances. They both found answers in biology’s most fundamental engine: mitochondria.
Their studies show how small changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of mitochondria can have huge physiological consequences that contribute to birds’ long-duration, continent-spanning flights.
“Exercise physiologists study the mitochondria because they provide the energy needed to maintain healthy cells, to maintain proper cellular function — but also, just in general, the energy we need to exercise,” Mesquita said. “That energy is what fuels movement.”

To Paulo Mesquita, an exercise physiologist, mitochondria are the center of the universe.
Courtesy of Paulo Mesquita/OMRF
These pioneering studies on mitochondrial performance and bird migration highlight the fact that a seasonal response to changing light levels, not physical preparation, triggers crucial subcellular changes, said
Wendy Hood
, who studies physiological ecology at Auburn University in Alabama; Mesquita worked with her and other colleagues on these questions during his graduate studies.
Humans “have to train for a while before we start to see any changes in the performance of our mitochondria,” she said. With migratory birds, “it’s spring, they get the right light cycles, and their body starts producing more and better, or higher-quality, mitochondria.”
The recent work advances the idea that there are significant ways in which an organism can change, without modifying its underlying genetic makeup, in response to its environment, said
Scott McWilliams
, a professor of wildlife ecology and physiology at the University of Rhode Island who was not involved in either study. This “phenotypic flexibility” in birds has been shown to vary according to seasons and population, and these studies are some of the first to demonstrate this across species and subspecies at the mitochondrial level.
“Such a theme,” he said, “is centrally important for understanding how birds during migration accomplish their athletic feats.”

主要讨论点：围绕医疗文档自动化、EHR（电子健康记录）系统集成以及医疗保险理赔优化的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ttcbj] 指出，其妻子所在的医院面临收入压力，而当前许多临床医生由于缺乏知识或未落实最佳实践，在文档记录中存在遗漏，导致无法使用高付费代码。虽然每年有一次关于如何通过文档记录提高收入的讲座，但并非所有医生都会参加，且没有量化改进的机制。
  
• [whitten] 提供了一个开放源代码的EHR/EMR系统——World VistA，并表示愿意帮助有兴趣的人进行集成。

• [candiddevmike] 对产品的实际应用提出疑问，特别是该工具是否需要医生离开EHR系统使用，并指出这可能会成为使用的重大障碍。

• [abelanger] 对拒保原因进行了探讨，询问文档错误与保险公司故意拒保的比例，并关注误报的检查过程。

• [arkmm] 提到医疗行业的繁文缛节使得初创公司难以在没有大量风投资金的情况下运营，并询问该公司如何找到初始用户以及为何选择从康复诊所开始。

• [shcheklein] 对产品未来发展表示期待，并希望看到其在医疗领域之外的应用。

• [vasusen] 关心医疗专业人员如何查看和批准文档的更改，以及EHR工具中是否存在版本控制。

• [hooverd] 对PowerChart和Epic的集成体验提出质疑，认为其界面设计存在问题。

• [sigmaisaletter] 提到该产品似乎仅限于美国市场，并询问在GDPR规定更严格的欧盟是否可行。

• [aerhardt] 询问代理是否全部基于LLM（大型语言模型），还是使用了其他AI/ML技术。

• [w10-1] 建议将Epic IT集成商作为目标客户，并指出EHR系统的UI设计存在重大问题，导致医疗工作流程复杂化。其认为AI在EHR系统中的应用应着重于改进UI/UX，而非仅仅增加理赔收入。此外，提出应开发一个AI测试工具来评估Epic系统的可用性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是文档记录中的遗漏与保险公司故意拒保的比例，以及如何有效减少拒保的发生。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是EHR系统的界面问题，以及如何通过AI技术改善用户体验和系统可用性。
• 不同市场（如美国与欧盟）在医疗数据处理上的法规差异对产品推广的影响也被提及。

这些讨论显示了医疗文档自动化和EHR系统集成的复杂性，以及在不同应用场景中面临的挑战和机遇。

data.title: The Soviet People's Car: The Enduring Legacy of the Lada
data.author: jruohonen
data.article_summary: 《苏联国民车：拉达的持久遗产》文章简要总结了拉达汽车的历史和影响。20世纪60年代，苏联与意大利菲亚特公司合作，引进了先进汽车技术，打造了适应本国条件的拉达2101车型。这款车简单耐用，价格实惠，迅速成为苏联人民的国民车，象征着新的社会流动性和国家自豪感。随后推出的拉达Niva在国内外市场也大获成功，成为苏联出口的盈利产品，扩展了其国际影响力。尽管苏联解体，拉达品牌依然存在，全球销量超过2000万辆，并在俄罗斯市场占有重要地位。然而，其安全性能曾受到批评。

44081130.article_content:
The Soviet People’s Car: The Enduring Legacy of the Lada
The Lada wasn’t just a car—it was a Soviet statement. Rugged, practical, and iconic, it symbolised national pride and outlived the USSR itself.
A model poses with a Lada VAZ-2101 at Big Almaty Lake, (1980s), Almaty, Kazakh SSR.
Credit: Lada Archive
At the height of the Cold War, scientists on both sides of the Atlantic were locked in a race to build bigger, more powerful rockets. The Soviet Union had just sent the first human to space.
Space was the future. Compared to that, cars felt archaic. But for the USSR, mass-producing a Soviet car wasn’t just about transportation—it was a matter of national pride.
The Birth of the Lada
In 1966, the Soviet government
partnered with Italian car manufacturer
Fiat to create the Lada. This was a rare instance of technological cooperation between the USSR and a Western company.
The partnership gave the Soviet Union access to advanced automotive technology while maintaining the illusion of self-sufficiency. It was a statement: the USSR could develop and manufacture consumer goods that could stand alongside those from the West.
An advertisement for Lada exports, (1970s).
Credit: Lada Archive
Modeled on the Fiat-124, the result was the Lada 2101. But before it could hit Soviet roads, it had to be
adapted for local conditions
. Engineers reinforced the suspension to handle unpaved roads, strengthened the body to withstand harsh winters, and added extra rust protection to combat road salt. The engine and mechanical components were also simplified so that owners could repair them easily, even in remote areas with no access to service centers.
In 1970, the first Lada rolled off the AvtoVAZ production line. Unlike the Model T, which came in any color as long as it was black, the Lada was available in
two colours
—red and blue, the colors of the RSFSR flag.
It was an instant success. Affordable, reliable, and easy to fix, the Lada became the car of the Soviet people. Demand far outstripped supply, with wait times stretching
several years
unless you had connections in the government. Despite this, AvtoVAZ launched its first advertising campaign that same year.
A Car for the People, By the People
The Lada 2101 became a cultural icon. For millions of Soviet citizens, it was their first car, a symbol of newfound mobility. Its simplicity and durability made it beloved, while its impact on Soviet society extended far beyond transportation.
An advertisement for the VAZ-2101, (1970s), Russian SFSR.
Credit: Lada Archive
It appeared in music, film, and literature. Vladimir Vysotsky’s 1972 song
Dialogue by the TV
humorously captured the long wait times: “I’ve been in line for a car for five years, but it’s not a waste—I’m saving up!”
The 1979 comedy
Garage
, directed by Eldar Ryazanov, used the struggle for garage spaces to highlight the Lada’s place in Soviet life. In Viktor Pelevin’s novel
Omon Ra
, the Lada served as both a symbol of Soviet progress and its limitations.
Other nations had their own iconic vehicles. Germany had the Volkswagen Beetle, a symbol of postwar recovery. Italy’s Fiat 500 embodied the country’s economic boom and
La Dolce Vita
era. Britain’s Mini captured the spirit of the swinging '60s. Like these, the Lada was more than just a car—it was a cultural cornerstone.
A Rural Workhorse in the Lada Niva
A year after the Lada 2101 debuted, Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin
ordered AvtoVAZ to create a rugged vehicle
for the countryside. The result was the Lada Niva, borrowing elements from another Fiat, the 127.
LADA Niva Advertisement (1977), Russian SFSR.
Credit: LADA Archive
Before production began in 1977, the Niva was
tested in the harshest conditions
imaginable—the Ural Mountains, the barren landscapes of Siberia, and the vast deserts of Kazakhstan. It didn’t just survive; it thrived.
The Niva was another success, quickly capturing more than
40% of Europe's 4x4 market
. The Lada brand became one of the Soviet Union’s most profitable exports—a rolling ambassador of Soviet ideology.
Ladas
made for export
were of superior quality, with thicker metal, reinforced transmissions, and better batteries. The cars reached Cuba, India, Egypt, and Eastern Europe, extending Soviet influence in a way that was both economic and symbolic. 44081130.article_summary: 《苏联国民车：拉达的持久遗产》文章简要总结了拉达汽车的历史和影响。20世纪60年代，苏联与意大利菲亚特公司合作，引进了先进汽车技术，打造了适应本国条件的拉达2101车型。这款车简单耐用，价格实惠，迅速成为苏联人民的国民车，象征着新的社会流动性和国家自豪感。随后推出的拉达Niva在国内外市场也大获成功，成为苏联出口的盈利产品，扩展了其国际影响力。尽管苏联解体，拉达品牌依然存在，全球销量超过2000万辆，并在俄罗斯市场占有重要地位。然而，其安全性能曾受到批评。

data.title: Bits with Soul
data.author: mrkeen
data.article_summary: 在达尔文学院的访谈中，计算机科学家Simon Peyton Jones分享了他对编程语言研究的见解。他讨论了函数式编程的重要性，特别是Haskell语言的开发和应用。Jones强调编程语言对软件可靠性和开发效率的影响，并解释了纯函数式编程如何通过避免副作用来提高代码质量。他还谈到了在学术界和工业界之间架起桥梁的必要性，以促进新技术的发展和应用。Jones的讲座为听众提供了对编程语言设计深刻而实用的理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学的教育和其在社会中的作用

不同观点：
• 观点一：计算机科学不仅仅是对技术能力的培养，而是通过编码和数字技术为人们提供了一种全新的理解和探索世界的方式。通过将信息数字化，人们可以进行机械化的分析和转换，探索传统手工方法无法实现的领域。例如，程序的复杂性可以与人类最复杂的艺术品相媲美，但仅需一个USB驱动器即可存储。这一观点强调了计算机科学的创造性和探索性。

• 观点二：计算机科学与日常生活紧密交织，理解其工作原理、其擅长的领域以及可能出现的失败情况，对于现代人的生存和发展至关重要。因此，计算机科学教育应当成为每个孩子教育的一部分。这一观点强调了计算机科学教育的必要性和普及性，认为它是现代社会不可或缺的技能。

• 观点三：计算机科学不仅仅是严肃的工程技术，它还具有快乐、美丽和创造性的一面。这一观点强调了计算机科学的美学和趣味性，认为它不仅是一种技术工具，更是一种艺术形式，能够带给人们乐趣和美感。

补充讨论：
评论中提到了对计算机科学的常见误解，即认为其从业者是社交能力不足的“书呆子”，在地下室中与冰冷的数字和屏幕为伍。然而，评论反驳了这种观点，强调了计算机科学的丰富性和创造性，以及其对社会生活的深远影响。争议的焦点可能在于计算机科学的公众形象与其真实本质之间的差距，以及如何有效地推广和普及这一学科的教育。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Dan Vanderkam解决Boggle问题的事件，各方对该问题的技术、难度、价值以及媒体报道的讨论。

不同观点：
• [smcin] 引用了Vanderkam的博客和他多年来独自研究Boggle问题的努力，强调了他对这一问题的持续关注和记录。Vanderkam认为自己是唯一对这个问题感兴趣的人。
• [robinhouston] 对这一技术故事被主流媒体（如《金融时报》）报道感到惊讶，并好奇该媒体如何发现这个故事，因为这类内容通常先在技术社区传播。
• [cgreerrun] 对Vanderkam使用的C++和Python组合以及pybind11工具表示赞赏，认为这种组合在快速原型和性能之间达到了良好的平衡。
• [throwaway81523] 对计算资源的成本和效率进行了分析，比较了Google Cloud的192核服务器与Ryzen 5950X及Epyc 7502P的性能和价格，指出不同硬件配置在处理时间上的可能差异。
• [sphars] 对Boggle问题的复杂性和Vanderkam在减少计算量上的成就表示钦佩，指出可能的组合数量巨大，解决问题所需的计算资源和时间也相当可观。
• [jebarker] 认为这个问题虽然看似简单，但其难度和Vanderkam的坚持令人钦佩，并将这种行为比作发现新最大梅森素数的努力，认为这是被技术问题吸引并愿意投入时间和金钱的表现。

补充讨论：
• [everyone] 提出了在Scrabble和Boggle游戏中，追求分数最大化与使用优雅词汇之间的张力，表达了对游戏中使用不雅词汇的看法。
• [38] 仅提出了对镜像链接的请求，未深入讨论。

争议焦点：
• 对于Boggle问题的价值和关注度存在不同看法。Vanderkam认为自己是唯一感兴趣的人，而其他人则认为这是一个有趣且值得关注的问题。
• 对计算资源和效率的评估存在技术性讨论，特别是不同硬件配置在处理类似问题上的性价比分析。

data.title: Tachy0n: The Last 0day Jailbreak
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Siguza在2020年发现并利用的一个iOS内核漏洞（tachy0n），该漏洞影响了iOS 13.0至13.5，并在unc0ver v5.0.0中发布。这是当时一个罕见的0day漏洞，因为苹果在一周后为此专门发布了补丁。作者解释了这个漏洞的发现过程，以及它如何通过回归测试被重新找到。漏洞存在于lio_listio系统调用中，涉及一个竞态条件，导致内核内存重复释放，从而可以被利用进行内核权限提升。这个漏洞的特殊之处在于它曾被当作1day使用过，但由于苹果的疏忽，它未被完全修复，最终成为0day。作者还回顾了类似漏洞的历史，如SockPuppet，强调了苹果在回归测试方面的不足。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果设备的漏洞发现与修补过程，以及围绕 jailbreak 的技术与经济问题。

不同观点：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 认为苹果在漏洞修补和回归测试方面存在不足，特别是在 iOS 12.4 中重复出现了之前已经被修补的漏洞（SockPuppet）。他推测这是因为苹果缺乏有效的回归测试机制，并提出可以通过自动化测试历史漏洞的方式来发现新的漏洞。这种方法在其他开源项目（如 Linux、FreeBSD 等）中可能也具有潜力。

• [0x38B] 对技术细节（如 kheap 分离、task port 缓解措施等）表示困惑，并用比喻说明对 jailbreak 技术讨论的理解困难。他还提到自己对 jailbreak 的兴趣主要来自娱乐性，而非实用性，并抱怨由于其开发者账号问题，无法使用一些 jailbreak 工具如 UTM。

• [weinzierl] 提到苹果目前对 jailbreak 漏洞的收购价格至少为一百万美元。这表明苹果对 jailbreak 漏洞的重视，并通过高额奖励来鼓励发现和报告漏洞。

• [ivanjermakov] 认为苹果通过封锁设备 root 权限的方式，成功地将 jailbreak 开发者发现的漏洞免费修补，这是一种聪明的策略。这暗示苹果可能在利用外部开发者社区的力量来强化其系统安全。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于苹果是否有效修补了所有已知漏洞，以及他们是否依赖外部开发者的 jailbreak 来改进其系统安全。
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 强调了自动化回归测试的重要性，并质疑其他开源项目是否也采用类似方法来发现潜在漏洞。
• [0x38B] 的评论更多是个人经历与感受，特别是对 jailbreak 工具使用中的实际问题，如账号限制等，提出了不满。
• [weinzierl] 和 [ivanjermakov] 则讨论了苹果在经济和策略层面上如何应对 jailbreak 漏洞，以及这种策略的潜在效益。

44083388.article_content:
Siguza, 23. May 2025
tachy0n
The last 0day jailbreak.
0. Introduction
Hey.
Long time no see, huh?
People have speculated over the years that someone “bought my silence”, or asked me whether I had moved my blog posts to some other place, but no. Life just got in the way.
This is not the blog post with which I planned to return, but it’s the one for which all the research is said and done, so that’s what you’re getting. I have plenty more that I wanna do, but I’ll be happy if I can even manage to put out two a year.
Now,
tachy0n
. This is an old exploit, for iOS 13.0 through 13.5, released in
unc0ver
v5.0.0 on May 23rd, 2020, exactly 5 years ago today. It was a fairly standard kernel LPE for the time, but one thing that made it noteworthy is that it was dropped as an 0day, affecting the latest iOS version at the time, leading Apple to
release a patch
for just this bug a week later. This is something that used to be common a decade ago, but has become extremely rare - so rare, in fact, that is has never happened again after this.
Another thing that made it noteworthy is that, despite having been an 0day on iOS 13.5, it had actually been exploited before - by me and friends - but as a 1day at the time. And that is where this whole story starts.
In early 2020,
Pwn20wnd
(a jailbreak author, not to be confused with Pwn2Own, the event) contacted me, saying he had found an 0day reachable from the app sandbox, and was asking whether I’d be willing to write an exploit for it. At the time I had been working on
checkra1n
for a couple of months, so I figured going back to kernel research was a welcome change of scenery, and I agreed. But where did this bug come from? It was extremely unlikely that someone would’ve just sent him this bug for free, with no strings attached. And despite being a jailbreak author, he wasn’t doing security research himself, so it was equally unlikely that he would discover such a bug. And yet, he did.
The way he managed to beat a trillion dollar corporation was through the kind of simple but tedious and boring work that Apple sucks at: regression testing.
Because, you see: this has happened before. On iOS 12,
SockPuppet
was one of the big exploits used by jailbreaks. It was found and reported to Apple by
Ned Williamson
from Project Zero, patched by Apple in iOS 12.3, and subsequently unrestricted on the Project Zero bug tracker. But against all odds, it then resurfaced on iOS 12.4, as if it had never been patched. I can only speculate that this was because Apple likely forked XNU to a separate branch for that version and had failed to apply the patch there, but this made it evident that they had no regression tests for this kind of stuff. A gap that was both easy and potentially very rewarding to fill. And indeed, after implementing regression tests for just a few known 1days, Pwn got a hit.
So just for a moment, forget everything you know about kheap separation, forget all the task port mitigations, forget SSV and SPTM… and let’s look at some stuff from the good old times.
1. Lightspeed
First, a quick recap on this bug. This is the
Lightspeed
bug from Synacktiv (CVE-2020-9859 and possibly CVE-2018-4344). It’s in the
lio_listio
syscall, which lets you do asynchronous and/or batched file I/O. To keep track of all submitted I/O ops, the kernel allocates this struct:
struct
aio_lio_context
{
int
io_waiter
;
int
io_issued
;
int
io_completed
;
};
The actual work is then performed on a separate thread, which is also responsible for freeing this struct once all I/O has been completed (in
do_aio_completion
):
/* Are we done with this lio context? */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
lio_context
->
io_completed
)
{
lastLioCompleted
=
TRUE
;
}
/*
* free the LIO context if the last lio completed and no thread is
* waiting
*/
if
(
lastLioCompleted
&&
(
waiter
==
0
))
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
But in the case where
nothing
has been scheduled at all, that code path will never be hit, and so the
current
thread has to free this struct again, right from
lio_listio
:
case
LIO_NOWAIT
:
/* If no IOs were issued must free it (rdar://problem/45717887) */
if
(
lio_context
->
io_issued
==
0
)
{
free_context
=
TRUE
;
}
break
;
if
(
free_context
)
{
free_lio_context
(
lio_context
);
}
The problem is just that this check is racy. If work
has
been submitted to the other thread, but it has
already completed
by the time this check runs, then
lio_context
is a dangling pointer here. You can check the
original blog post
for more details, but in order to exploit this, we want the following sequence of events:
lio_listio
allocates
lio_context
.
The work completes and
do_aio_completion
frees
lio_context
.
We reallocate the freed memory with something we control, such that
lio_context->io_issued == 0
.
lio_listio
sees
lio_context->io_issued == 0
and frees our allocated object.
We reallocate it again with something else, and now have two entirely different allocations pointing to the same memory.
Now, we’re targeting 64

• [ivanjermakov] 认为苹果通过封锁设备 root 权限的方式，成功地将 jailbreak 开发者发现的漏洞免费修补，这是一种聪明的策略。这暗示苹果可能在利用外部开发者社区的力量来强化其系统安全。

• [weinzierl] 和 [ivanjermakov] 则讨论了苹果在经济和策略层面上如何应对 jailbreak 漏洞，以及这种策略的潜在效益。

data.title: Please Fund More Science (2020)
data.author: ssuds
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了结束新冠疫情、恢复正常生活的三种可能途径：开发出有效疫苗使病毒基本停止传播，找到有效治疗方法使人们不再恐惧，或建立完善的检测、追踪、戴口罩和隔离文化。作者认为，目前政府对研发的资助不足，私营部门和慈善机构虽能部分填补空缺，但并非长久之计。然而，生物科技公司和研究实验室正以惊人速度专注于解决这一问题，展现出空前的创新精神。作者呼吁投资者和捐赠者将更多资源投入科学研究，以应对当前及未来的疫情。这不仅有助于解决问题，还能带来新的机遇和乐观情绪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技精英与科学基金资助、新冠疫情的应对方式、私人和公共科研资助的比较与重要性

不同观点：
• Havoc认为科技精英正在资助的机构正在削减国家科学基金会（NSF）的资金，这具有讽刺意味。他引用了《纽约时报》的一篇文章来支持自己的观点，指出NSF正面临资金被大幅削减的困境。

• Yegg提供了十一个理由来支持科学资助的必要性，包括延长寿命、国防安全、经济回报、创新驱动、环境需求等。他认为这些理由足以说明科学资助的重要性，尤其是在多方面的回报上。

• WorkerBee28474认为新冠疫情并没有通过疫苗、治疗或测试追踪等方式结束，而是因为人们不再关心疫情而结束。这种观点强调了社会对疫情态度的转变，而非科学解决方案的实现。

• Petermcneeley支持WorkerBee28474的观点，并引用比尔·盖茨的文章，指出疫情实际上是通过第四种方式解决的，即变得像季节性流感一样。

• Jun8提出少数富人可以通过早期发掘人才、资助暑期学校、建立研究中心、设立大奖等方式对科学发展产生巨大影响。他详细描述了具体措施，并认为这些措施的成本相对较低，但效果显著。

• Babuloseo分享了自己利用加密货币挖矿剩余的GPU参与Folding@Home项目的经历，认为这种做法有助于科学研究，虽然个人贡献有限。

• EricDeb认为私人资助可能建立更好的激励机制，但公共研究的减少仍然令人遗憾，显示出对公共资助科研的重视。

• Toddm用Frank Zappa的名言讽刺硅谷文化，希望像Altman这样的人只是历史中的注脚，而不是像Frank Zappa那样成为永恒的头条。

• Light_hue_1认为这些超级富豪实际上并没有为科学提供多少资助，Altman和OpenAI、Google、微软等公司在这方面的贡献微乎其微，尽管这些公司有能力增加基础科学资助。

• PaulKeeble强调仍需开发能阻止新冠传播和治疗长新冠的疫苗，指出随着时间的推移，情况变得越来越严重，而政治决策导致资金大幅减少，呼吁更多关注和投入。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科技精英和超级富豪是否应该且实际对科学资助的贡献大小，以及公共和私人资助在科研中的角色和重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及了应对新冠疫情的不同方式，特别是社会态度转变与科学解决方案的对比。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何通过早期发掘和培养人才、设立激励机制等方式有效推动科学进步，以及这些措施的可行性和成本效益。

44082968.article_content:
Experts on the COVID-19 pandemic seem to think there are three ways out—that is, for life, health, and the economy to return roughly to normal.
Either we get a vaccine good enough that R0 for the world goes below 1, a good enough treatment that people no longer need to be afraid, or we develop a great culture of testing, contract tracing, masks, and isolation.
I wish that the federal government were doing much more—it would be great to see even a few percent of the recent stimulus bill go to funding R+D.  But they don’t seem to be funding enough science, and although I think concerns about the private sector and philanthropy doing what the government is supposed to be doing are somewhat valid, there isn’t a great alternative right now.
On the positive side, I have never seen a field focused on one problem with such ferocity before.  The response of biotech companies and research labs is amazing, and the speed they are operating at seems to have increased by more than 10x.  It’s the best of the spirit of innovation, and it’s inspiring to see what these companies and research labs are doing.
Scientists can get us out of this.  What they need are money and connections.
Investors and donors—this is where we can help.  Please consider shifting some of your focus and capital to scientific efforts addressing the pandemic.  (And future pandemics too—I think this will be a before-and-after moment in the world, and until we can defend against new viruses quickly, things are going to be different.)
The learning curve is quick, and there are a lot of experts willing to help you with diligence.  It feels good to do something that might be useful, it’s interesting to do something totally new, and it will make you more optimistic.
If you make it known to your network that you want to fund efforts working on COVID-19, you’ll get flooded with opportunities.  And it’s always good to invest where the best founders are congregating.

data.title: Reinvent the Wheel
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“不要重复造轮子”这句常见建议的局限性，认为鼓励探索和好奇心更为重要。文章指出，通过亲手实现和创造可以加深对技术的理解，即使最终不使用自己的成果，过程中也能学到很多。作者以轮子为例，说明重新发明可以带来更好的解决方案、帮助学习、解决问题以及激发创新。文章最后建议，为了获得洞见可以重新造轮子，而在追求实际影响时则应重用现有成果。作者还推荐了CodeCrafters平台以提升编程技能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该重新发明轮子（reinvent the wheel）

不同观点：
• **支持重新发明轮子**：
   - **学习与理解**：重新发明轮子是深入理解技术概念的有效方法，尤其是从基础原理开始构建能够增强对技术的掌握（[megadragon9], [gfalcao], [richardjennings]）。
   - **创新与创造**：重新发明轮子可以带来新的视角和创新，甚至可能创造出比现有技术更好的解决方案（[boricj], [gfalcao] 的引用）。
   - **避免不必要的依赖**：通过重新发明轮子，可以避免引入过多的外部依赖，从而简化系统（[begueradj]）。

• **反对盲目重新发明轮子**：
   - **时间和资源限制**：在工作环境或创业公司中，重新发明轮子可能会浪费宝贵的时间和资源，尤其是在有现成且成熟的解决方案时（[mullingitover], [dustingetz], [kayodelycaon]）。
   - **生产环境中的风险**：除非重新发明的轮子在质量和功能上能超越现有方案，否则在生产环境中使用可能带来风险（[wcfrobert], [kayodelycaon]）。

• **中立或条件支持**：
   - **时机和目的**：重新发明轮子应根据具体情况决定，特别是在学习或需要定制解决方案时是有意义的，但在商业项目中需谨慎（[wcfrobert], [richardjennings]）。
   - **理性决策**：团队应合理评估是否需要重新发明某些组件，避免陷入“非我发明”（Not Invented Here）综合症，但同时也应考虑市场现有方案的兼容性和成本（[awinter-py]）。

补充讨论：
• **哲学与社会批判**：有评论提到现代社会对冗余的过度排斥可能限制了个人创造力和多样性（[ppqqrr]）。
• **学习前人的工作**：在重新发明轮子之前，应先了解已有的工作，以避免重复劳动并从中获得启发（[cryptonector]）。
• **具体案例**：一些评论者分享了个人经验，如构建自定义机器学习库，展示了重新发明轮子的实际学习效果（[megadragon9]）。

争议焦点：重新发明轮子在学习和创新中的价值与其在实际项目中可能带来的时间和资源消耗之间的平衡。

44083467.article_content:
Published on 24th of May, 2025
Reinvent the Wheel
Tagged with
dev
culture
One of the most harmful pieces of advice is to not reinvent the wheel.
It usually comes from a good place, but is typically given by two groups of people:
those who tried to invent a wheel themselves and know how hard it is
those who never tried to invent a wheel and blindly follow the advice
Either way, both positions lead to a climate where curiosity and exploration gets discouraged. I’m glad that some people didn’t follow that advice; we owe them many of the conveniences of modern life.
Even on a surface level, the advice is bad: We have much better wheels today than 4500–3300 BCE when the first wheel was invented. It was also
crucially
important that wheels got reinvented throughout civilizations and cultures.
Note:
When I say “wheel” throughout this post, please replace it with whatever tool, protocol, service, technology, or other invention you’re personally interested in.
Inventing Wheels Is Learning
“What I cannot create, I do not understand”
–
Richard Feynman
, Physicist and Nobel Prize Winner
To
really
understand something on a fundamental level, you have to be able to implement a toy version first. It doesn’t matter if it’s any good; you can throw it away later.
In Computer Science, for example, there are many concepts that are commonly assumed to be beyond the abilities of mere mortals: protocols, cryptography, and web servers come to mind.
More people should know how these things work. And therefore I think people should not be afraid to recreate them.
Everything Is A Rabbit Hole
Too often, fundamental things are taken for granted. For example strings or paths are super complicated concepts in programming. It’s a great exercise to implement a string or a path library yourself if you’re interested in how they work.
Even if nobody ends up using your work, I bet you’ll learn a lot. For example:
There is an infinite complexity in everyday things.
Building something that even a single other person finds useful is a humbling experience.
Humans like you created these abstractions. They are not perfect and you can make different tradeoffs in your own design.
On the last point, everything is a tradeoff and there are dozens, sometimes hundreds of footguns with every toy problem.
Along the way, you will have to make decisions about correctness, simplicity, functionality, scalability, performance, resource usage, portability, and so on.
Your solution can be great in some of these things, but not all of them and not for all users. That also implies that existing solutions have flaws and might not be designed to solve your particular problem; no matter how well-established the solution is.
Going down rabbit holes is fun in its own way, but there is one other benefit: It is one of the few ways to level up as an engineer… but only if you don’t give up before you end up with a working version of what you tried to explore. If you jump between projects too often, you will learn nothing.
Reasons for Reinventing the Wheel
There are great reasons to reinvent the wheel:
Build a better wheel (for some definition of better)
Learn how wheels are made
Teach others about wheels
Learn about the inventors of wheels
Be able to change wheels or fix them when they break
Learn the tools needed to make wheels along the way
Learn a tiny slice of what it means to build a larger system (such as a vehicle)
Help someone in need of a very special wheel. Maybe for a wheelchair?
Who knows? The wheel you come up with might not be the best use for a car, but maybe for a… skateboard or a bike? Or you fail building a nicer wheel, but you come up with a better way to test wheels along the way. Heck, your wheel might not even be meant for transportation at all! It might be a potter’s wheel, “a machine used in the shaping (known as throwing) of clay into round ceramic ware”
according to Wikipedia
. You might end up building a totally different kind of wheel like a steering wheel or a flywheel. We need more people who think outside the box.
Reuse vs Reinvent
Of course, don’t disregard the works of others – study their work and reuse where you see fit. Don’t reinvent the wheel out of distrust or ignorance of the work of others. On the other side, if you never tried to put your knowledge to the test, how would you ever learn enough about your field to advance it?
I observed you can move very quickly by running little experiments. Especially in software engineering, building small prototypes is cheap and quick. Solve your own problem, start small, keep it simple, iterate.
So, with all of the above, here’s my advice:
Reinvent for insight. Reuse for impact.

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了后末日科幻设定中车辆战争的后勤问题，以《疯狂麦克斯》（特别是《狂暴之路》和《芙里欧萨》）为例，分析了此类作品中车辆战争的模式及其在后勤方面的可行性。作者指出，这类作品通常展现大规模的摩托车、肌肉车和武装卡车战争，强调高速战斗。作者对比了其他末日设定，如《辐射》和僵尸题材作品中车辆使用的不同，并提出大规模社会在进行车辆战争时需要进行大量改装。文章进一步探讨了这种战争模式在后勤和战术上的问题，并提出更合理的替代方案，同时反思现代军事后勤。最后，作者邀请读者支持其项目，并可通过电子邮件或社交媒体获取更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于现代与历史战争中的车辆使用及其有效性的讨论，以及在不同背景下的技术自主性问题。

不同观点：
• sndean认为，《伟大的丰田战争》中展示的非对称战争非常有趣，尤其是查德用轻型车辆如Hiluxes和Land Cruisers对抗利比亚的坦克。他将这种现象类比为现代战争中无人机的作用，强调了技术和战术的演变。

• Animats推荐了《The Angry Staff Officer》博客，该博客由现役军官撰写，提供专业分析，内容涵盖从星战到巴比等流行文化作品中的军事视角，为对这种分析感兴趣的人提供了额外资源。

• gamescr讨论了《辐射》游戏中的车辆问题，指出在现代《辐射》游戏中，地面车辆的缺失是由于游戏机制和引擎限制，而非技术问题。他还提到，过多的障碍和毁坏的道路使得地面车辆难以实现，并且车辆会使游戏世界显得更小。

• rasz提到了2024年俄罗斯瓦格纳在非洲的行动，作为支持步兵对抗重型武装车队的例子，提供了现代战争中的另一个论据，表明简单的步兵配置有时能有效对抗高度武装的车队。

• johnea对技术自主性提出了批评，质疑在类似《Mad Max》的背景下谁在提炼汽油，并指出电力的重要性。他认为，农村居民由于文化战争中的立场而拒绝电气化，导致他们继续依赖石油开采和提炼行业，限制了他们的技术自主性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的技术和战术的演变，特别是从历史战争（如丰田战争）到现代无人机战争的类比。
• 游戏中车辆使用的实际限制和设计选择，特别是游戏机制对世界构建的影响。
• 技术自主性在现实世界中的重要性，尤其是在农村地区和后末日背景下的能源选择问题。

争议焦点：
• 关于在不同背景下（电影、游戏、现实战争）车辆和技术自主性的实际效用和可行性的不同看法。
• 农村居民对电气化的拒绝是否合理，以及这种拒绝是否会削弱他们的技术自主性。

44083580.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
May 23, 2025
33 Minutes
This week, we’re doing another ‘silly’ topic, but this being me, it is a silly
logistics
topic, because – as the saying goes – amateurs talk tactics, professionals talk logistics.  So we’re going to be
professionally
silly this week and talk about
the logistics of vehicle warfare in a post-apocalyptic sci-fi setting
, in part because this is a good way to also think about why militaries (of various description) use the vehicles they use, from a logistics standpoint.
Our pop-culture starting point here is
going to be the ‘Mad Max’ universe
and similar settings (
Rage
, the recent
Badlands Crew
,
Fallen Earth
etc), particularly the vision of motorized post-apocalyptic warfare that emerges quite clearly from
Mad Max: Fury Road
and
Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga
.
1
I should note that while I’m treating
Mad Max
as a single setting here, I’m going to focus a lot more on
Fury Road
and
Furiosa
, because those are the films that feature the most large-scale warfare (though we’ll get a few mentions of
Mad Max 2
as well). We’ll outline in a moment the overall warfare ‘model’ these settings use, but what I find particularly notable are the vehicles used: often large numbers of motorcycles and motorbikes, muscle cars and the distinctive presence of ‘war rigs’ – massive weaponized trucks – and the assumption that a lot of the fighting is conducted ‘at speed.’
Of course that’s not the only vision for vehicles in the post-apocalypse. In some settings, vehicles figure in only a little: in the modern
Fallout
games
2
the only vehicles of gameplay import are aircraft.  The existence of ground vehicles is implied in dialogue, but we never see them, presumably because they’d be too difficult to implement in the engine.  Zombie fiction often features small groups of survivors in individual civilian vehicles, sometimes hardened for combat, but typically not (and often when they are hardened, it is for ‘ramming’ crowds, which is not a thing that would be good to modify a civilian vehicle for).
I want to focus on the
Mad Max
-style settings because they feature larger factions engaging in warfare at a variety of scales with modified and even purpose-built vehicles.  We wouldn’t expect small survivor groups weeks or months after some form of the apocalypse to be significantly modifying their vehicles
but we would
expect substantial modifications to be made by full societies engaging in warfare at scale with these vehicles.  Also, again, it’s a fun setting.
So what we’ll do is outline the ‘warfare model’ of these
Mad Max
-style settings, discuss the problems with that warfare model and then lay out a more plausible replacement and in the process think a bit about modern military logistics.
Of course, building an army of improved fighting vehicles to rove the
wasteland
internet searching for resource rich convoys and settlements to plunder doesn’t come cheap, so if you like what you are reading, you can help by sharing it so that we can assemble the largest possible post-apocalyptic road-warrior band.  If you really like it, you can help support the project on
Patreon
.  I can’t promise to use your support to mount heavy weapons to the top of my Honda Civic, but I also won’t promise
not
to do that.  And if you want updates whenever a new post appears, you can click below for email updates or follow me on
Twitter
and
Bluesky
and (less frequently) Mastodon (@bretdevereaux@historians.social) for updates when posts go live and my general musings; I have largely shifted over to Bluesky (I maintain some
de minimis
presence on Twitter), given that it has become a much better place for historical discussion than Twitter.
Email Address
Subscribe!
The
Mad Max
Warfare Model
We want to start by laying out what I am going to call the ‘
warfare model
‘ of the setting.
When I say ‘warfare model’ here, what I mean is how a fictional setting imagines warfare to be conducted
across all of the different levels of military analysis
.  Put simply
how does warfare work in this setting?
So the ‘warfare model’ is a big collection of smaller models, like a ‘strategic model’ (what aims are pursued by war in the setting and how) or the ‘tactical model’ (how does battle with these weapons actually work) and so on.  For this post, we’re really interested in the tactical and logistical models, but I want to start by outlining in a basic way the whole ‘vision’ and how within the fiction it fits together.
This is, I think, a particularly handy framework to think about in science fiction, because while
fantasy
works often implicitly borrow a lot of their warfare model from pre-modern history, science fiction settings do not.  They may feature radically alien war aims, logistics or tactics, predicated on equally unusual technologies or conditions.
Fortunately for us, the
Mad Max
warfare model is not so alien, though it does have quirks.  Warfare in these settings is waged principally over resources, primarily four: water, fo

data.title: Postgres IDE in VS Code
data.author: Dowwie
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VS Code中Postgres支持的最新扩展及其相关工具的比较与争议

不同观点：
• **支持VS Code数据库扩展的观点**：
  - [seveibar] 认为该扩展解决了其npm包"pgstrap"试图解决的问题，即提供数据库模式的上下文，方便LLM和代码审查。不过其对是否应让编辑器具有数据库感知功能持不确定态度，担心生成代码过多。
  - [alexpham14] 表示感谢，认为该扩展对使用VS Code和Postgres的开发者非常有用，但对优先支持Postgres感到意外。

• **对VS Code和数据库工具的比较**：
  - [impalallama] 认为JetBrains的集成数据库工具更胜一筹。
  - [qntmfred] 表示对Postgres的工具生态不满，认为SSMS更符合其习惯。
  - [FajitaNachos] 和 [pamelafox] 提到Postico和现有工具如DBeaver也是流行的选择。

• **对非VS Code用户的影响和跨平台支持的质疑**：
  - [WuxiFingerHold] 质疑该扩展是否仅限于VS Code，是否能在Neovim等其他编辑器中使用，并对Microsoft的专有性表示担忧。
  - [pbw] 询问SQLite支持情况，关注是否需要为每个数据库单独开发扩展。

• **对微软战略的讨论**：
  - [Toritori12] 讨论VS Code和Visual Studio的市场定位变化，认为VS Code已成为主流IDE。
  - [ryanmccullagh] 引用“拥抱、扩展、消灭”策略，暗示对微软扩展策略的潜在担忧。

补充讨论：
• **跨多显示器使用的需求**：[bdcravens] 提到希望VS Code能更好地支持多显示器工作流。
• **对微软限制的疑虑**：[mohsen1] 担心微软可能限制VS Code分支使用某些扩展。
• **对其他数据库扩展的需求**：[zamacho] 询问是否有类似的MySQL扩展。

争议焦点：VS Code Postgres扩展的专有性、对非VS Code用户的影响以及微软在开发工具市场的战略意图。

data.title: Use ramoops for logging under Linux (2021)
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Linux系统中使用ramoops记录崩溃日志。ramoops驱动可以将内核崩溃信息、控制台输出和用户消息存储在RAM中的预留内存区域，以便在重启后进行分析。相比于闪存，RAM速度更快且不会耗尽持久存储空间，但数据在断电后会丢失。文章以Toradex的Apalis iMX8QM为例，展示了如何通过修改设备树预留1MB的RAM用于日志记录，并配置ramoops参数（如记录大小、控制台输出大小和用户消息大小）。最后，还需要确保内核配置中启用了pstore和ramoops模块，Toradex提供的iMX8内核默认已启用这些选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：pstore（persistent storage）在不同平台和场景下的应用和重要性

不同观点：
• [remram] 认为 pstore 具有多种后端支持（如ACPI和UEFI变量），虽然不一定在所有嵌入式平台上都有，但在某些关键时刻可能是唯一的救命稻草。他分享了一个实际案例，在处理集群中机器随机重启的问题时，正是通过 pstore 读取了内核崩溃日志，才发现问题根源是一个Ceph bug，而非电源问题。

• [tripdout] 指出，在Android设备上，如果没有串行控制台，pstore 是获取Android启动前崩溃日志的最佳方法，因为此时logcat还无法 streaming 日志。这强调了 pstore 在移动设备调试中的实用性。

补充讨论：
• pstore 作为一种持久化存储机制，在不同平台（如嵌入式系统、服务器集群、Android设备）上都展示了其独特的价值，尤其是在传统日志获取方式不可用的情况下。

• 实际案例展示了 pstore 的关键作用：[remram] 的经验说明了在服务器环境中排查内核崩溃问题时，pstore 提供了至关重要的信息；[tripdout] 的评论则突显了 pstore 在移动设备调试中的不可或缺性。

争议焦点：
• 评论之间并没有明显的争议，更多的是从不同角度（服务器集群与Android设备）强调了 pstore 的实用性和重要性。

Contents
Use ramoops for logging under Linux
Stefan Eichenberger
2021-04-07
1721 words
9 minutes
Contents
Unfortunately, an embedded system is not free of crashes. To analyze and log such crashes it is useful to have a file system where we can store such information between reboots. One interface which is meant to do that is
pstore
and its current single implementation
ramoops
. Ramoops can store log messages inside a reserved memory area in RAM. The nice thing about RAM is, that it should almost always be available when the CPU is still running. Flash memory on the other hand could not be available because e.g. the eMMC or NAND flash driver crashed. Further, by using RAM instead of flash memory we can write faster and don’t fill our persistent memory. The disadvantage of storing information in RAM is that the information will not survive a power cycle.
For this article an
Apalis iMX8QM from Toradex
was used with
Reference Multimedia Image 5.1.0
.
Ramoops
The ramoops driver allows us to store kernel oopses, the kernel console output and user messages in a reserved memory region inside RAM. In normal hardware designs RAM will not power off when we just do a reboot and therefore the data will survive a restart. By defining a reserved memory region the kernel will not touch this memory area and therefore not overwrite data stored there. We have to find a free memory region in RAM which we can use. For this we read /proc/iommem on the device.
root@apalis-imx8:~$ cat /proc/iomem
....
80200000-83ffffff : System RAM
80280000-8161ffff : Kernel code
81620000-8188ffff : reserved
81890000-81a85fff : Kernel data
86400000-87ffffff : System RAM
90000000-901fffff : System RAM
90500000-91ffffff : System RAM
94c00000-94ffffff : System RAM
95400000-ffffffff : System RAM
96000000-d1ffffff : reserved
f9603000-fd62afff : reserved
880000000-8ffffffff : System RAM
8fae00000-8fb5fffff : reserved
8fb7fe000-8ff5fffff : reserved
8ff6db000-8ff73afff : reserved
8ff73b000-8ff73bfff : reserved
8ff73c000-8ff7cbfff : reserved
8ff7ce000-8ff7cefff : reserved
8ff7cf000-8ff7d3fff : reserved
8ff7d4000-8ff7d4fff : reserved
8ff7d5000-8ffffffff : reserved
We see that there are other memory regions marked as reserved. This regions are used e.g. for interprocessor communication. We just need to choose a region which is not used already. Let us pick an area of 1MB right at the start of the second RAM bank at 0x880000000. We now need to add that region to reserved-memory inside the device tree. Let us do that step by step.
Enable Ramoops
We first checkout the kernel.

build@machine:~$
cd
linux-toradex

44082544.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Linux系统中使用ramoops记录崩溃日志。ramoops驱动可以将内核崩溃信息、控制台输出和用户消息存储在RAM中的预留内存区域，以便在重启后进行分析。相比于闪存，RAM速度更快且不会耗尽持久存储空间，但数据在断电后会丢失。文章以Toradex的Apalis iMX8QM为例，展示了如何通过修改设备树预留1MB的RAM用于日志记录，并配置ramoops参数（如记录大小、控制台输出大小和用户消息大小）。最后，还需要确保内核配置中启用了pstore和ramoops模块，Toradex提供的iMX8内核默认已启用这些选项。
44082544.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：pstore（persistent storage）在不同平台和场景下的应用和重要性

不同观点：
• [remram] 认为 pstore 具有多种后端支持（如ACPI和UEFI变量），虽然不一定在所有嵌入式平台上都有，但在某些关键时刻可能是唯一的救命稻草。他分享了一个实际案例，在处理集群中机器随机重启的问题时，正是通过 pstore 读取了内核崩溃日志，才发现问题根源是一个Ceph bug，而非电源问题。

• [tripdout] 指出，在Android设备上，如果没有串行控制台，pstore 是获取Android启动前崩溃日志的最佳方法，因为此时logcat还无法 streaming 日志。这强调了 pstore 在移动设备调试中的实用性。

补充讨论：
• pstore 作为一种持久化存储机制，在不同平台（如嵌入式系统、服务器集群、Android设备）上都展示了其独特的价值，尤其是在传统日志获取方式不可用的情况下。

• 实际案例展示了 pstore 的关键作用：[remram] 的经验说明了在服务器环境中排查内核崩溃问题时，pstore 提供了至关重要的信息；[tripdout] 的评论则突显了 pstore 在移动设备调试中的不可或缺性。

争议焦点：
• 评论之间并没有明显的争议，更多的是从不同角度（服务器集群与Android设备）强调了 pstore 的实用性和重要性。

data.title: Is Astrophotography Without Tracking Possible? (2022)
data.author: astroimagery
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了无追踪设备下的天文摄影技巧，能够帮助拍摄者捕捉惊人的星空照片。通过选择明亮且固定的目标（如银河），使用稳固的三脚架，并应用如“500规则”等方法，可以在没有昂贵追踪设备的情况下拍得出色的夜景照片。对于广角镜头（17-24mm），限制曝光时间在15-20秒以内，并叠加数百张照片，可以创建清晰的银河图像。拍摄深空天体则需要更大镜头和更短的子曝光时间。如果没有追踪器，曝光时间应控制在20-30秒以内，以避免星轨现象。文章还提到，选择高亮度目标（如猎户座星云）可以无需追踪器，而暗弱天体则需要更长曝光和追踪设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：天文摄影中无跟踪拍摄的可行性及相关技术

不同观点：
• [hengheng] 认为现代天文摄影多指广角地景上的星空摄影，而非深空摄影（如星云、星系等）。无跟踪广角拍摄在技术上已经可行，尤其是随着镜头和传感器技术的进步，15秒的曝光已经足够展示星空。但在某些情况下，曝光需要堆叠，而地景和天空的堆叠常常会导致不自然的照片。深空摄影的吸引力正在减弱，因为网上已有高质量的图片，且这些图片缺乏摄影师的个人故事。

• [pppone] 指出在天文学研究中，已经存在无跟踪拍摄的成功案例，例如“南极天目计划”利用漂移扫描CCD技术实现了无跟踪拍摄。这表明在专业领域，无跟踪技术已经得到了应用。

• [jameslk] 认为无跟踪天文摄影的主要用例之一是利用如Siril等软件进行堆叠处理。这类工具可以帮助处理无跟踪拍摄中的多张照片，以提高最终成像质量。

• [incomingpain] 强调在需要15秒曝光的情况下，跟踪仍然是必要的。新的天文摄影技术更注重快速曝光，以最大化利用良好的大气条件，而不是依赖长曝光。

• [shmerl] 提出使用Dobsonian反射望远镜是否能捕捉更多光线，从而减少曝光时间的要求。这暗示了不同设备在无跟踪拍摄中的潜在优势。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多种技术手段和工具，如漂移扫描CCD、堆叠软件（如Siril），这些都在无跟踪天文摄影中扮演重要角色。
• 讨论还涉及了深空摄影与广角星空摄影在情感和故事性上的区别，指出深空摄影可能缺乏个人故事和背景，从而降低了对普通摄影爱好者的吸引力。
• 争议的焦点之一是无跟踪拍摄在不同情况下的可行性，特别是曝光时间和跟踪需求的讨论。

44049965.article_content:
Astrophotography
Astrophotography Without Tracking: How to Capture Amazing Photos
Posted by
Karl Perera MA
–
November 30, 2022
Table of Contents
Astrophotography without tracking is absolutely possible and can produce stunning results with the right techniques. By choosing bright and stationary targets like the Milky Way, using a sturdy tripod, and applying methods like the 500 Rule, you can capture breathtaking night sky photos without the need for expensive tracking equipment. This guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master astrophotography without tracking, even as a beginner.
You can do astrophotography without a star tracker by attaching a DSLR camera to a sturdy tripod
1
. This will limit the length of your exposures to 15-20 seconds. With a lens of 17–24mm
,
stacking hundreds of photos will create a good image of the Milky Way. Deep Sky targets need bigger lenses and shorter subs.
If you want to take amazing photos of the night sky without tracking, you need an astrophotography DSLR camera with a wide-angle lens.
Check out this Canon EOS Rebel T7 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm Lens
(shop now at Amazon)
and see the difference.
We do need to look into this question much deeper because there are many variables that can make astrophotography harder without a star tracker mount. There is a lot more to answering this entirely, so stick with me. This page is filled not only with what you need to know but also with what I have learned through my own experience and research into this question of tracking.
Why Might We Use Tracking?
The reason we need a star tracker mount is that astronomical objects in the sky are moving, generally from east to west, depending on where in the sky the object or star is within our solar system. This movement occurs because our planet is rotating. In the Northern Hemisphere, where I live, stars and other objects in the sky seem to rotate around a point near Polaris, the North Star which we can also call the Polar Axis.
In order to counteract the rotation of the stars, we need to use a star tracker mount that follows the movement of the stars and moves in the opposite direction to keep the object in the centre of the field of view
Telescope, DSLR and AZ-ALT tracking mount
Another reason we use a star tracker mount is to enable us to take long exposures to photograph faint objects in the sky and capture their fine details. Without a star tracker, we will get star trails and blurry images with less detail. Most telescopes, but not all, are sold with a tracking mount, but you can also buy a portable star tracker such as the Sky-Watcher Star Adventurer.
Star Adventurer Tracking Mount
Includes counterweight, CW bar, tripod, and pier extension
Goto system
Lightweight
Great product!
Buy from Amazon
As an Amazon associate I earn a small commission, thanks for your support!
Astrophotography without tracking is possible, but then we are limited to exposures no longer than about 30 seconds.
My research into this revealed that I could take up to 20-second exposures with a 17 or 24-mm lens on my astrophotography DSLR, a Canon 600D, with no star tracker as I attempted to image the Milky Way, resulting in less noise. This was possible because my target was generally high in the sky. I couldn’t see any trailing in the stars despite not using a tracker mount.
In March 2022, I went to Bali and
experimented with astrophotography using a 50mm focal
length lens and a DSLR with a tripod to photograph the Orion Nebula and Horsehead Nebula. I took 435 5-second exposures. Although the picture came out brilliantly on close inspection when zoomed in, the stars were trailing slightly even after 5 seconds of exposure time!
Orion Nebula shot by Karl Perera in Bali 435 x 5 sec.
When I photographed these two objects, I noticed they were low on the horizon and eventually heading towards setting. This may have been a reason why even 5 seconds of astrophotography without tracking was still causing small amounts of star trailing.
The 500 rule
explains how long we can expose without star trails.
What is your Astrophotography Target?
Whether or not you can image the night sky without a star tracker depends on your target. Some targets, such as deep sky objects such as galaxies and nebulae, are so far away that they are extremely faint, so hours of long exposure times are usually necessary. For extremely difficult-to-image targets, it is best to use longer exposures in the minutes to get a quality image, but you can image these with much shorter untracked images if you take hundreds or even thousands of photos.
The target mentioned above, the Orion nebula, is very bright and not so far away, so short exposures can work. So to capture these kinds of bright targets, you do not need to use tracking.
Galaxies, apart from Andromeda, which is both massive and can be seen with the naked eye in dark skies, need longer exposures of one minute or more and several hours of exposure.

data.title: Solving the mystery of a dinosaur mass grave at the 'River of Death'
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 在加拿大阿尔伯塔省的皮普斯通溪（昵称“死亡之河”），古生物学家正在挖掘一个7200万年前的恐龙大规模墓地，试图解开这些恐龙如何死亡的谜团。数千只名为厚鼻龙（Pachyrhinosaurus）的恐龙被瞬间埋葬在这里，这个墓地被认为是北美最大的骨床之一。挖掘工作显示，每平方米可能包含多达300块骨头，化石密度惊人。研究人员认为，这些恐龙可能是在迁徙途中遭遇灾难。除了厚鼻龙，该地区还发现了其他大型恐龙的遗骸，如埃德蒙顿龙（Edmontosaurus），帮助科学家重建这片古老土地的生态系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dinosaur National Monument的Bone Quarry及其科学、情感和文化意义

不同观点：
• [somat的观点] Bone Quarry的参观体验近乎宗教体验。somat在没有事先研究的情况下去参观，原本期待只是一个大型化石，但实际看到大量化石时感到震撼。他对化石被分散到多个博物馆展示感到矛盾，一方面认为能让更多人分享这一伟大发现，另一方面也对化石未能完整保留感到遗憾。somat还幽默地建议“Bone Quarry”可以作为金属乐队的名字。

• [kulahan的观点] 强调了Bone Quarry的科学价值。kulahan指出，大多数已知恐龙物种仅根据单一标本描述，而Bone Quarry却拥有数千个Pachyrhinosaurus标本，显示了该地的珍贵。这种丰富性填补了恐龙研究中的许多空白，使得Bone Quarry成为科学研究的宝库。

• [shadowsharp的观点] 将Bone Quarry与John Reeves在阿拉斯加发现的boneyard相比较，指出了两者在化石发现方面的相似性。虽然没有详细展开，但这种比较暗示了不同地点在古生物学发现上的共同价值。

补充讨论：
• somat对化石展示方式的复杂情感引发了对化石保护和展示策略的思考，即如何在科学研究和公众教育之间取得平衡。
• kulahan对化石数量和其科学意义的关注强调了Bone Quarry在填补恐龙研究空白方面的独特贡献。
• shadowsharp的比较提示了全球范围内类似化石遗址的重要性，以及这些遗址在古生物学研究中的普遍价值。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在化石的展示和保护策略上，somat对化石分散展示感到矛盾，而kulahan则侧重于化石的科学价值和研究贡献。这反映了公众对化石遗址利用方式的不同期望和优先考虑。

44053110.article_content:
Solving the mystery of a dinosaur mass grave at the 'River of Death'
6 days ago
Share
Save
Rebecca Morelle
Science editor
Reporting from
Alberta, Canada
Alison Francis
Senior science journalist
Share
Save
A tour of the bones being unearthed at Pipestone Creek
Hidden beneath the slopes of a lush forest in Alberta, Canada, is a mass grave on a monumental scale.
Thousands of dinosaurs were buried here, killed in an instant on a day of utter devastation.
Now, a group of palaeontologists have come to Pipestone Creek - appropriately nicknamed the "River of Death" - to help solve a 72-million-year-old enigma: how did they die?
Trying to work out exactly what happened here starts with the hefty strike of a sledgehammer.
Brute force is needed to crack open the thick layer of rock that covers what Professor Emily Bamforth, who's leading the dig, describes as "palaeo gold".
As her team begins the more delicate job of removing the layers of dirt and dust, a jumble of fossilised bones slowly begins to emerge.
Kevin Church/BBC News
A hip bone of a Pachyrhinosaur is one of thousands of discoveries in the creek
"That big blob of bone right there is, we think, part of a hip," Prof Bamforth says, watched on by her dog Aster - whose job today is to bark if she spots any nearby bears.
"Then here, we have all of these long, skinny bones. These are all ribs. And this is a neat one - it's part of a toe bone. This one here, we have no idea what it is - it's a great example of a Pipestone Creek mystery."
BBC News has come to Pipestone Creek to witness the sheer scale of this prehistoric graveyard and see how researchers are piecing together the clues.
Thousands of fossils have been collected from the site, and are constantly generating
new discoveries
.
Kevin Church/BBC News
Prof Bamforth's dog, Aster, on lookout duties
The bones all belong to a dinosaur called Pachyrhinosaurus. The species, and Prof Bamforth's excavation, feature in a new landmark BBC series - Walking With Dinosaurs - which uses visual effects and science to bring this prehistoric world to life.
These animals, which lived during the Late Cretaceous period, were a relative of the Triceratops. Measuring about five metres long and weighing two tonnes, the
four-legged beasts had large heads
, adorned with a distinctive bony frill and three horns. Their defining feature was a big bump on the nose called a boss.
The dig season has just started and lasts each year until autumn. The fossils in the small patch of ground that the team are working on are incredibly tightly packed; Prof Bamforth estimates there are up to 300 bones in every square metre.
So far, her team has excavated an area the size of a tennis court, but the bed of bones extends for a kilometre into the hillside.
"It's jaw dropping in terms of its density," she tells us.
"It is, we believe, one of the largest bone beds in North America.
"More than half of the known dinosaur species in the world are described from a single specimen. We have thousands of Pachyrhinosaurus here."
Kevin Church/BBC News
Pipestone Creek still holds many secrets
Palaeontologists believe the dinosaurs were migrating together in a colossal herd for hundreds of miles from the south - where they had spent the winter - to the north for the summer.
The area, which had a much warmer climate than it does today, would have been covered in rich vegetation, providing abundant food for this enormous group of plant-eating animals.
"It is a single community of a single species of animal from a snapshot in time, and it's a huge sample size. That almost never happens in the fossil record," says Prof Bamforth.
Walking with Dinosaurs/BBC Studios
Pachyrhinosaurus had distinctive unicorn-style horns, as shown in this computer-generated image
Bigger beasts offering clues
And this patch of north-western Alberta wasn't just home to Pachyrhinosaurus. Even bigger dinosaurs roamed this land, and studying them is essential to try and understand this ancient ecosystem.
Two hours drive away, we reach the Deadfall Hills. Getting there involves a hike through dense forest, wading - or doggy-paddling in the case of Aster - across a fast-running river, and clambering over slippery rocks.
No digging is required here; super-sized bones lie next to the shoreline, washed out from the rock and cleaned by the flowing water, just waiting to be picked up.
A huge vertebra is quickly spotted, as are bits of ribs and teeth scattered across the mud.
Kevin Church/BBC News
A toe bone found in the Deadfall Hills, home to the Edmontosaurus
Palaeontologist Jackson Sweder is particularly interested in what looks like a chunk of dinosaur skull. "Most of what we find here is a duck-billed dinosaur called Edmontosaurus. If this is a skull bone, this is a dinosaur that's large - probably 30ft (10m) long," he says.
The Edmontosaurus, another herbivore, roamed the forests like the Pachyrhinosaurus - and is helping palaeontologists build up a picture of this ancient land.
Sweder is the co
44053110.article_summary: 在加拿大阿尔伯塔省的皮普斯通溪（昵称“死亡之河”），古生物学家正在挖掘一个7200万年前的恐龙大规模墓地，试图解开这些恐龙如何死亡的谜团。数千只名为厚鼻龙（Pachyrhinosaurus）的恐龙被瞬间埋葬在这里，这个墓地被认为是北美最大的骨床之一。挖掘工作显示，每平方米可能包含多达300块骨头，化石密度惊人。研究人员认为，这些恐龙可能是在迁徙途中遭遇灾难。除了厚鼻龙，该地区还发现了其他大型恐龙的遗骸，如埃德蒙顿龙（Edmontosaurus），帮助科学家重建这片古老土地的生态系统。

data.title: What I discovered when I asked Amazon to tell me everything Alexa had heard
data.author: robaato
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者与Amazon Alexa智能音箱的多年互动经历，以及他请求亚马逊提供所有Alexa收集到的家庭数据后的发现。作者描述了Alexa如何成为家中的多功能助手，但也指出了其局限性，比如音乐品味有限、对法语口音不友好等。通过下载的数据，作者看到了所有购买记录、Kindle阅读历史、视频观看记录，以及与Echo的所有对话和请求。尽管数据繁杂，文件命名不清晰，但通过分析文本数据，作者能够快速了解家庭使用Alexa的模式，如常播放的音乐和常问的问题。最终，作者对这些数据感到释然，尽管Alexa多年来一直在“窃听”家庭生活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能音箱（如Amazon Echo）的隐私问题及其在家庭中的使用对隐私的影响

不同观点：
• [threeducks] 认为，通过Alexa设备收集的数据包含了家庭成员的私密信息，特别是其女儿Coco搜索敏感话题（如“全性恋”和“全知”）的记录。这种信息本应是私密的，而现在却被公开披露，甚至发表在新闻文章中，这侵犯了隐私，越过了道德界限。

• [rainsford] 指出，人们与Alexa等语音助手互动时，有一种奇怪的拟人化倾向，这种现象与人们通过语音与设备交互的方式有关，而不是仅仅因为数据被收集。文章中提到的Coco与Alexa的“关系”被描述为一种特殊的人际互动，但这种现象在文章中没有被深入探讨。此外，rainsford认为，由于语音交互的自然性，人们可能将技术视为更具人性化，但实际上这些设备并不真正具有人类智能。

• [throwaway81523] 认为，Alexa设备不应被称为“家用音箱”，而应被称为“家用麦克风”，因为它的主要功能是收集声音信息，而非播放音频内容，这反映了其作为监听设备的本质。

• [andix] 表示惊讶，因为之前不知道Amazon会保存所有与Alexa的对话记录，这种做法被认为是不寻常且值得关注的。

• [aunty_helen] 对人们在家中，尤其是孩子床边放置主动监听的设备表示不信任和反对，认为这种行为与他们对互联网服务提供商的不信任类似，都是对隐私的潜在威胁。

• [Animats] 提到，不仅公司会收集这些数据，国土安全部（Homeland Security）也能查看所有这些信息，进一步引发了对隐私和数据安全的担忧。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于智能音箱设备是否在家庭中扮演了过度侵入的角色，尤其是在涉及到儿童的隐私时。
• 人们与语音助手之间的互动方式，以及这种互动是否导致了对技术智能性的误解，也是一个值得深入探讨的话题。
• 数据安全和政府机构对这些数据的访问权限增加了对隐私问题的复杂性。

Illustration: Steven Gregor/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Illustration: Steven Gregor/The Guardian
Amazon Alexa
‘Alexa, what do you know about us?’ What I discovered when I asked Amazon to tell me everything my family’s smart speaker had heard
For years, Alexa has been our on-call vet, DJ, teacher, parent, therapist and whipping boy. What secrets would the data reveal?
Jeremy Ettinghausen
Sat 24 May 2025 06.45 EDT
Last modified on Sat 24 May 2025 11.57 EDT
Share
S
he is always listening. She is unfailingly polite. She is often obtuse. She is sometimes helpful. She frequently frustrates. She isn’t great with bashment artists. Or grime. Or drum’n’bass. She needs to be spoken to slowly and clearly, as you’d talk to an aged relative with diminished faculties. She doesn’t like French accents.
‘“Alexa, how long do wasps live for?”
“Alexa, how long do wasps live if you hit them with a tea towel and then a saucepan?”
In September 2016, a new presence appears in our house, squatting on the kitchen counter between the kettle and the coffee machine. It is blandly futuristic, a minimal cylinder with an LED ring that glows blue to alert us to the fact that it is ready, poised to answer our questions or carry out our instructions, as long as those instructions are clearly stated and fall within a narrow band of available “skills”.
More often than I’d like, the solid blue glow is replaced by a rotating wash of green to tell us that an
Amazon
order is on its way. Occasionally, the light is red: this happens when someone has turned off the microphone to seize control of the device and impose their music on all of us. Our Amazon Echo is primarily used as the family Bluetooth speaker, and a glance through the music played on it demonstrates that there is very little common ground between our differing tastes. In a household with three young people, the kitchen is a place of musical education and dispute, with the Echo the communal weapon of choice.
Our Echo is one of the early ones: essentially a smart speaker connected to a server where the fairly rudimentary Alexa voice assistant attempts to turn our requests and questions into actions and answers. More recent incarnations have screens that allow you to make video calls or stream TV programmes, inevitably, through Amazon Prime. And, when Amazon releases its long-awaited, generative AI-enabled update in the next few weeks or months, my aged unit will be incompatible with Alexa+. It won’t remember my favourite movies or meals, and it won’t help me plan a night out or book an Uber or find a babysitter. But given what Alexa (and, by extension, Amazon) has heard and analysed and stored in the nine years they have been eavesdropping on us, I am happy to settle for our first-generation Echo’s more limited capabilities.
Our requests ranged from prosaic to troubling and downright bizarre – there was very little we didn’t ask Alexa
Last year, I realised that my relationship with Amazon predated my mortgage, my marriage, parenthood, two distinct careers and a host of other significant life moments. To see if I could distil anything of value – the contours of a 21st-century adulthood, perhaps – from all the information Amazon holds about me, I requested all the available data using
an almost impossible to find link
. Would I be reassured or disturbed when I found out what Amazon and Alexa knew about my family?
A couple of days later, I received an email containing links to gigabytes of information: particulars of every purchase I’ve ever made – from the noir novel I bought on the day that Amazon UK launched to the 28th pair of headphones acquired in as many years. Records of every page turn of every Kindle ebook I’ve opened, every moment of Prime content I’ve watched, measured by the second. And, of course, the details of every interaction we have ever had with our Echo; every question asked, every song requested, every timer set.
They don’t make it easy to find gold among the fields of data available for download. Folder and file names are opaque and unhelpful. Competence with spreadsheets is useful and a subscription to a powerful AI assistant is advantageous. Time and patience are necessary. One folder contains nothing but thousands and thousands of sound files, all with the same date and each with a nonsensical string of characters instead of a name. It is definitely fun to click on these at random and hear the voices of various family members mispronouncing band names, asking for Pokémon jokes or demanding that Alexa “play a fart noise”. But without any semblance of order to the files, going through 15,000 of them (“Alexa, never mind”) would truly be a sisyphean task. Or a briefly entertaining family parlour game.
Fortunately, along with the sound files, Amazon provides spreadsheets and spreadsheets of text-based data that reduces the amount of time needed to assess our Alexa usage from months to days. Using these spreadsheets and searching for the word “play”, I can see t

data.title: voyage-3.5 and voyage-3.5-lite: improved quality for a new retrieval frontier
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: Voyage AI推出了最新一代嵌入模型voyage-3.5和voyage-3.5-lite，相较于前代模型voyage-3和voyage-3-lite，新模型在检索质量上有所提升，且价格不变。它们支持2048、1024、512和256维的嵌入，并通过Matryoshka学习和量化感知训练实现多重量化选项。与OpenAI-v3-large相比，voyage-3.5和voyage-3.5-lite的检索质量分别提高了8.26%和6.34%，同时成本降低了2.2倍和6.5倍。与Cohere-v4相比，voyage-3.5也表现更优。新模型在多领域评估中表现出色，并通过改进的训练数据混合和Voyage AI的重新排序器进一步提升了性能。评估结果显示，它们在技术文档、代码、法律、金融等多个领域均有显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Voyage和Gemini等嵌入模型在性能、可靠性及应用场景方面的比较

不同观点：
• [__jl__] 认为Voyage模型在实际使用中表现出色，特别是3.5-lite版本因其价格优势而备受关注。然而，对Voyage API的不可靠性及其被MongoDB收购后的发展方向表示担忧。此外，对Google的Gemini嵌入模型持观望态度，质疑其更新频率及Google对嵌入模型的长期承诺。

• [kaycebasques] 关注Voyage-3.5和Gemini Embedding模型在检索任务上的表现对比，质疑Voyage-3.5是否只在特定数据集上优于OpenAI和Cohere模型，还是在所有检索任务上都占据领先地位。此外，还讨论了Voyage模型是否仅适用于检索任务，而非 clustering 或 STS 等任务。

• [serjester] 提出嵌入模型性能可能已经达到饱和的观点，认为在实际应用中，大多数人只关注前50个候选结果的重排序，因此1-3%的性能提升并不显著。主张当前的重点应是缩小模型规模以降低托管成本。

• [greenavocado] 询问Voyage模型与BGE M3模型的比较，关注不同模型之间的性能和应用差异。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多个模型在不同任务上的性能对比，如Voyage-3.5与Gemini Embedding、OpenAI及Cohere模型，以及BGE M3模型。
• 讨论了模型性能的实际应用价值，包括检索任务的局限性和性能提升的边际效益。
• 关注模型的小型化和成本效益，反映了用户对实际应用中经济因素的重视。
• 对Google等大公司在嵌入模型上的长期承诺和更新频率表示关注，反映了用户对技术支持和持续发展的期望。

TL;DR – We’re excited to introduce
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
, the latest generation of our embedding models. These models offer improved retrieval quality over
voyage-3
and
voyage-3-lite
at the same price, setting a new frontier for price-performance. Both models support embeddings in 2048, 1024, 512, and 256 dimensions, with multiple quantization options enabled by Matryoshka learning and quantization-aware training.
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
outperform OpenAI-v3-large by 8.26% and 6.34%, respectively, on average across evaluated domains, with 2.2x and 6.5x lower respective costs and a 1.5x smaller embedding dimension. Compared with OpenAI-v3-large (float, 3072),
voyage-3.5
(int8, 2048) and
voyage-3.5-lite
(int8, 2048) reduce vector database costs by 83%, while achieving higher retrieval quality.
Today, we’re excited to introduce
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
, which maintain the same sizes as their predecessors—
voyage-3
and
voyage-3-lite
—but offer improved quality for a new retrieval frontier.
As we see in the figure below,
voyage-3.5
improves retrieval quality over
voyage-3
by 2.66%, and
voyage-3.5-lite
improves over
voyage-3-lite
by 4.28%—both maintaining a 32K context length and their respective price points of $0.06 and $0.02 per 1M tokens.
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
also outperform OpenAI-v3-large by 8.26% and 6.34%, respectively, with
voyage-3.5
also outperforming Cohere-v4 by 1.63%.
voyage-3-lite
achieves retrieval quality within 0.3% of Cohere-v4 at 1/6 the cost. Both models advance the cost-performance ratio of embedding models to a new state-of-the-art through an improved mixture of training data, distillation from
voyage-3-large
, and the use of Voyage AI rerankers.
Matryoshka embeddings and quantization.
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
support 2048, 1024, 512, and 256 dimensional embeddings enabled by
Matryoshka learning
and multiple embedding quantization options—including 32-bit floating point, signed and unsigned 8-bit integer, and binary precision—while minimizing quality loss. Compared with OpenAI-v3-large (float, 3072),
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
(both int8, 2048) reduce vector database costs by 83%, while achieving outperformance of 8.25% and 6.35% respectively. Further, comparing OpenAI-v3-large (float, 3072) with
voyage-3.5
and
voyage-3.5-lite
(both binary, 1024), vector database costs are reduced by 99%, with outperformance of 3.63% and 1.29% respectively.
Evaluation Details
Datasets.
We evaluate on 100 datasets spanning eight domains: technical documentation, code, law, finance, web reviews, multilingual, long documents, and conversations. Each dataset consists of a corpus (e.g., technical documentation, court opinions) and queries (e.g., questions, summaries). . Given a query, we retrieve the top 10 documents based on cosine similarities and report the
normalized discounted cumulative gain

data.author: jl
data.article_summary: 本文是作者在巴克内尔大学毕业典礼上的演讲摘要。作者恭喜2025届毕业生，并分享了自己毕业后的迷茫经历。他提到，毕业是人生轨道上的“最后一站”，此后没有固定的方向，需要自己探索。他将毕业生分为三类：已有明确计划的人、没有计划也不想有计划的人，以及希望有计划但还没有的人。他为第三类人提供建议：首先要意识到生活没有既定轨道，可以重新塑造自己。他建议不要被过去的失败束缚，要主动探索各种职业选择，通过与有趣的人交流来缩小选择范围，并要勇于面对 rejection。最终，作者通过找到自己感兴趣的创业领域，实现了自己的 ambitious 计划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：毕业后生活方向的选择与自我定位

不同观点：
• joshstrange等认为，许多人毕业后感到迷茫是因为他们习惯了生活有明确的目标（如小学到大学的"轨道"），而现实生活中并没有这样的固定轨道。大学毕业后突然没有了明确的"下一站"，导致很多人不知所措。joshstrange强调，这种"轨道"的消失其实是一种解放，让人可以自由选择方向，尽管这也伴随着恐惧。他批评教育体系没有让学生做好这种心理准备。

• w10-1扩展了"找到你的人群"这一概念，认为不仅仅是寻找机会，而是要找到你真正相信的东西，并在此基础上建立相互信任的关系。这个过程涉及承受拒绝和怀疑，同时需要建立自己的方向并让他人信任你。这种关系是双向的，不仅仅是寻找机会，而是建立共同的承诺和责任。

• neilv对"找到你的人群"提出了不同的理解，认为这不一定适用于所有人。他指出，对某些人来说，"你的人群"可能是一个安静的小镇，生活稳定，邻里友好，而不是一味追求大城市或高风险的创业机会。他强调，每个人的追求不同，"有趣的人"不一定是在创业或高风险领域中找到的。

• jamesgill引用了史蒂夫·乔布斯的话来支持文中的观点，强调生活是可以被改变和影响的，人们应该打破常规去创造自己的生活，而不是被现有的生活框架束缚。

• lucasfcosta赞同文中的观点，认为人们常常过于依赖自己的"身份"（如失败者或成功者），而忽视了具体情况的变化。他强调，失败是具体的，而不是整体的，应该从失败中学习而不是被其定义。

• FlamingMoe对"我没有关心的事情"这句话产生共鸣，认为这完美描述了许多人在成年初期的迷茫状态。

• nathan_compton对文中的"拒绝免疫"观点提出质疑，认为这种态度虽然对创业者很重要，但也可能导致混乱和破坏。他分享了自己在一个由这种态度的创始人领导的公司工作的负面经历。

• compumike回忆了自己在大学时的类似讨论，认为毕业后失去了一种生活节奏，需要通过周围的人来重新找到这种节奏。

• phkahler质疑文中的成功是否源于后见之明，询问作者是否是在成功后才认识到正确的选择。

• qntty认为文中的地铁比喻很贴切，但可能在年轻时不容易理解。

• rr808认为作者很幸运能在正确的时间和地点获得成功，但对新毕业生来说，目前并没有明显的"亮 spots"。

• raywu对作者表示感谢，分享了自己受作者书影响的职业轨迹。

• babyent强调了选择朋友的重要性，认为应该选择那些能给自己带来积极影响的人，而不是那些拖后腿的人。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到人际网络和朋友的选择对个人发展的重要性，强调了相互信任和共同成长的关系。
• 有人质疑文中的观点是否适用于所有人，特别是那些追求稳定生活的人，而不仅仅是创业或高风险领域的人。
• 对"拒绝免疫"的态度产生了争议，一方认为这是创业成功的关键，另一方则认为这种态度可能导致负面后果。

44074017.article_content:
Thank you to Bucknell University for inviting me to be this year's commencement speaker. And congratulations to the Class of 2025!
Watch the speech on YouTube
.
Thirty-two years ago I was sitting where you are now. At least, I assume I was. I can't really remember anything about my own graduation. I was too hung over.
The main thing I remember from that time in my life is that I had no plan. I had a degree in English, no job, and no idea what I even wanted to do. I would have liked to work hard on something I cared about. But I didn't have anything I cared about, and it took me a decade to find one.
Maybe I can help you do that faster. Maybe I can help you figure out what to work on.
You fall into three groups. Some of you already have all kinds of ambitious plans. You're already admitted to med school for the fall, or whatever. Others of you have no ambitious plans and no desire to have any. You just want to have a happy life, and that's cool. But in the middle, there's a group who wish they had ambitious plans, but don't. This speech is for you. I'm going to tell you how to get ambitious plans.
The first step is to realize that the subway stops here. Up to this point in life, most of you have been rolling on train tracks. Elementary school, middle school, high school, college—it was always clear what the next stop was. In the process you've been trained to believe something that’s not true: that
all
of life is train tracks. And there are some jobs where you can make it stay like train tracks if you want, but really today is the last stop.
This fact is so terrifying that a lot of people try to remain in denial about it. (I certainly did.) But it's also exciting. You can go in any direction now.
I didn't realize that, so I looked for more tracks. I looked for a job at a big, well-known company that I hoped would train me to do something, but I didn't know or care what, really, just so long as I was on some new set of tracks. The fall after graduation I was on the night shift at Fidelity Investments customer service, answering people's questions about why the value of their mutual fund went down.
This wasn't fun or interesting to me. So why did I do it? Two reasons: I didn't know any better, and I didn't think I had any particular aptitude for any kind of work, so I was delighted that anyone would pay me to do anything.
So I'm going to tell you about a trick you can pull right here at the point where the train tracks end. You can reinvent yourself. I wish I’d known I could do that. I was lazy in college and got bad grades. But the real problem was that I believed them: I believed that mediocre grades meant I was a mediocre person. And that stuck with me for years. I'm sure most of you have done better in school than I did, but maybe there are some of you who are feeling a little unsure of yourself. But here's the thing: you don't have to tell people that.
They
don't know. So if you want to, you can just decide to shift gears at this point, and no one's going to tell you you can't. You can just decide to be more curious, or more responsible, or more energetic, and no one's going to go look up your college grades and say, "Hey, wait a minute, this person's supposed to be a slacker."
If I'd known then what I know now, I'd have realized that there are many different kinds of jobs you can get after college, some much more interesting than others. And if I'd known I could be more ambitious, I would have tried to get one of the more interesting ones.
The truth is there are thousands of different places you could go work, and you have to consider them all and figure out which is the best. But that sounds impossible, right? You only had to choose between 60 different majors, and now you have to choose between thousands of different jobs? How do you even do that? The first step, is to acknowledge that you have to. You can't just drift into the open mouth of Fidelity, like I did.
Ok, then what? How do you search through thousands of options? To be honest, you can’t. You have to use some kind of trick for narrowing them down. My favorite trick is people. Talk to people. Get introduced to new people. Find the people that you think are interesting, and then ask what they're working on. And if you find yourself working at a place where you don't like the people, get out.
That was how I finally figured out what to work on. I found the
startup people
, and I realized that startups were what I was interested in. Once I did, I got more ambitious. I decided to write a book about startups. And having my own project made me even more ambitious. Finally I was working on something of my own! But most people I told about this project didn't get it. I wasn't an author or a startup person. How could I be writing a book about startups?
Which leads me to my final point about getting ambitious plans: you have to be immune to rejection. People are going to dismiss you at first. If that's enough to stop you, you're doomed. So you have to l

data.title: Bash implementation of Tabloid, the clickbait programming language
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Tabloid编程语言的Bash实现，名为"tabloid.bash"。Tabloid是一种以夸张、 clickbait 风格的语句编写程序的语言。该项目包含一个解释器（`runtabloid`）用于运行Tabloid程序，如示例中展示的加法和斐波那契数列计算。输出不仅给出计算结果，还伴随一系列模仿clickbait风格的语句。文章还展示了运行斐波那契程序的性能数据。项目代码托管在GitHub上，使用Shell编写，目前获得4颗星。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：点击诱饵标题风格的编程语言（Tabloid）的创意及其实际应用价值

不同观点：
• 观点一：Tabloid语言是一种有趣的创意，能够引发对传统编程语言的反思。支持者认为它通过夸张的语法和风格，讽刺了现代网络文化中的点击诱饵现象，具有一定的社会讽刺意义。例如，有评论提到这种语言让人思考编程语言设计中的形式与功能问题。

• 观点二：Tabloid语言不具备实际应用价值，只是一种噱头。反对者指出，这种语言过于注重表面效果，缺乏实际编程中的效率和可维护性。有评论认为，虽然有趣，但在真实开发环境中不具备可行性。

• 观点三：Tabloid语言可能对编程教育有帮助。一些评论者认为，这种夸张和有趣的编程方式可能吸引初学者，激发他们对编程的兴趣。通过新奇的方式让初学者更容易理解某些编程概念。

• 观点四：对Tabloid语言的性能和可读性表示担忧。有评论指出，这种语言的语法可能导致代码难以阅读和维护，并且可能会对性能产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论了Tabloid语言与其他实验性编程语言的比较，例如Brainfuck和莎士比亚编程语言（Shakespeare Programming Language），这些语言同样注重形式而非功能，但在特定领域或教育中可能有其价值。

• 争议的焦点在于Tabloid语言的实用性与娱乐性之间的平衡。一部分人认为编程语言应注重效率和实用性，而另一部分人则强调创新和趣味性在激发创意和教育中的重要性。

• 有人提出，Tabloid语言可能更适合作为一种艺术项目或概念验证，而不是一个实际开发工具。这种定位使其在编程社区中可能更具吸引力，但对于实际应用开发者而言，可能缺乏吸引力。

44083044.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Tabloid编程语言的Bash实现，名为"tabloid.bash"。Tabloid是一种以夸张、 clickbait 风格的语句编写程序的语言。该项目包含一个解释器（`runtabloid`）用于运行Tabloid程序，如示例中展示的加法和斐波那契数列计算。输出不仅给出计算结果，还伴随一系列模仿clickbait风格的语句。文章还展示了运行斐波那契程序的性能数据。项目代码托管在GitHub上，使用Shell编写，目前获得4颗星。

主要讨论点：点击诱饵标题风格的编程语言（Tabloid）的创意及其实际应用价值

不同观点：
• 观点一：Tabloid语言是一种有趣的创意，能够引发对传统编程语言的反思。支持者认为它通过夸张的语法和风格，讽刺了现代网络文化中的点击诱饵现象，具有一定的社会讽刺意义。例如，有评论提到这种语言让人思考编程语言设计中的形式与功能问题。

• 观点二：Tabloid语言不具备实际应用价值，只是一种噱头。反对者指出，这种语言过于注重表面效果，缺乏实际编程中的效率和可维护性。有评论认为，虽然有趣，但在真实开发环境中不具备可行性。

• 观点三：Tabloid语言可能对编程教育有帮助。一些评论者认为，这种夸张和有趣的编程方式可能吸引初学者，激发他们对编程的兴趣。通过新奇的方式让初学者更容易理解某些编程概念。

• 观点四：对Tabloid语言的性能和可读性表示担忧。有评论指出，这种语言的语法可能导致代码难以阅读和维护，并且可能会对性能产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论了Tabloid语言与其他实验性编程语言的比较，例如Brainfuck和莎士比亚编程语言（Shakespeare Programming Language），这些语言同样注重形式而非功能，但在特定领域或教育中可能有其价值。

• 争议的焦点在于Tabloid语言的实用性与娱乐性之间的平衡。一部分人认为编程语言应注重效率和实用性，而另一部分人则强调创新和趣味性在激发创意和教育中的重要性。

• 有人提出，Tabloid语言可能更适合作为一种艺术项目或概念验证，而不是一个实际开发工具。这种定位使其在编程社区中可能更具吸引力，但对于实际应用开发者而言，可能缺乏吸引力。

data.author: cactusplant7374
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一种简约、低消费、可能较为孤立的乡村生活的可行性和吸引力进行的讨论。

不同观点：
• **xp84**：支持低消费和简约生活的理念，但指出该生活方式忽略了社会联系的重要性。远离家人和朋友使得这种生活方式对很多人不切实际，尤其在交通成本高昂的情况下。
• **TrackerFF**：质疑乡村生活的实际操作性，尤其是医疗和交通问题。认为没有汽车在乡村生活会非常不便，且乡村的基础设施和就业机会有限。
• **probably_wrong**：批评文章对过去乡村生活的浪漫化，指出历史上乡村生活条件恶劣。认为文章的论点自相矛盾，不应美化艰苦的生活条件。
• **owenversteeg**：同意文章的主要前提，但指出乡村工作的社会地位和尊重度较低，与过去相比，现代乡村工作无法提供同样的社会认同感。
• **stickfigure**：认可低消费生活的可行性，但强调医疗保健是无法回避的问题。认为依赖公共医疗补助并不是一个可扩展的解决方案。
• **999900000999**：分享个人经验，认为即使没有汽车也可以在乡村生活，并指出乡村公交系统的经济和可靠性。
• **xeromal**：表达对乡村生活的向往，认为对于有远程工作的人来说，城市生活没有必要且成本高昂。愿意为了低成本生活而接受一定程度的自我依赖和孤立。
• **aeturnum**：认为文章的结论部分有道理，强调现代人对“老版美国梦”的误解。指出这种生活方式对大多数人没有吸引力，但对愿意自我依赖的人来说是可行的。
• **kixiQu**：质疑文章的写作目的和风格，认为文章试图通过文学手法影响读者，而不是提供实际建议。
• **energywut**：指出文章忽视了社会差异，认为某些群体（如LGBTQ+）在乡村可能面临歧视和排斥，使得这种生活方式对这些人不可行。
• **brokegrammer**：认为乡村生活会导致孤独感，对心理健康不利，尤其对年轻人来说。强调社交联系的重要性，认为城市生活更有利于建立社交网络和职业发展。
• **Version467**：认为文章的数学计算方向正确，但生活方式的选择因人而异。对孤独和缺乏医疗保健表示担忧，但认为这种生活方式对某些人仍有吸引力。
• **lwansbrough**：批评文章建议年轻人放弃城市生活，选择贫困的乡村生活。认为这是一种倒退，而不是进步。
• **egypturnash**：认为乡村生活的艰苦条件（如气候）对某些人来说是优点，因为这减少了竞争，使得那些适应这种生活的人可以享受更多的资源。
• **kristianc**：批评文章表面上拒绝现状，实际上是接受现状并建议人们逃避到尚未受影响的地方。认为这种做法无助于改变现状。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要在于乡村生活的实际可行性和吸引力，包括社会联系、医疗保健、交通、社会认同和心理健康等方面。
• 个人经验和背景对这种生活方式的看法有很大影响，例如是否拥有汽车、是否需要定期医疗、是否有远程工作机会等。
• 文章的浪漫化和现实之间的差距也是讨论的一个重要方面，许多评论者指出历史上乡村生活的艰苦条件，并对文章的美化倾向提出批评。
• 社会差异和包容性问题也被提及，某些群体在乡村可能面临歧视和排斥，使得这种生活方式对他们不可行。

data.title: Why I no longer have an old-school cert on my HTTPS site
data.author: mcbain
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ACME协议及其相关工具的复杂性和实现问题

不同观点：
• eadmund认为，JSON在处理大整数时存在问题，因为JSON解析器可能无法正确处理大数，这会导致安全隐患。为了确保大整数的正确传输，使用Base64编码是一个合理的选择，但这样会牺牲JSON的可读性。总体上，JSON不如XML，更不如Canonical S-expressions。
• mcpherrinm作为Let’s Encrypt的技术负责人，承认ACME和JWS格式非常复杂，且由于IETF标准和委员会设计的原因，导致协议设计不如人意。但他提到一些库可以改善体验，尤其是在RESTful环境中的应用。
• 1a527dd5对ACME工具有实际使用经验，认为尽管ACME实现存在问题，但仍能找到合适的工具（如Crypt-LE、lego、Posh-ACME等）来完成任务。他强调，问题不在于ACME概念，而在于其实现。
• Arnavion基于自身经验，认为从零实现ACME客户端并不困难，并提供了相关博客文章作为参考，帮助简化理解RFC文档的流程。
• liampulles关注协议复杂性带来的“监管捕获”问题，认为复杂的协议可能导致只有大公司才能满足运行互联网的标准，中小型开发者会遇到更多困难。
• donnachangstein提到OpenBSD有一个轻量级的ACME客户端，符合Unix哲学，并建议如果现有工具不符合需求，可以尝试移植这个客户端。
• ddtaylor提到某些ACME客户端在处理公钥指数时存在编码错误，这可能导致意外问题，但仍然被广泛使用。
• arkadiyt从安全角度指出，使用4096位的RSA密钥会降低网站访问速度，且只提供2048位的安全强度，因此建议使用2048位的RSA密钥。
• jeroenhd认为，虽然手动实现ACME客户端可以增加经验，但作者对协议的厌恶情绪过于明显，并建议使用轻量级的ACME库来简化工作。
• pornel解释了数字以特定格式存储的原因，主要是因为证书中的DER编码和OpenSSL API使用这种格式，且为了处理长位数的数字，保持格式一致是合理的。
• red_admiral主张使用Ed25519密钥代替RSA，因为前者参数少、密钥短、格式简单，并避免了网络字节序问题，同时批评ECDSA过于复杂且容易出错。
• chrisweekly对ACME协议的复杂性表示震惊，并详细列举了涉及的多种技术和流程，认为这个协议是一个巨大的复杂谜团。
• gr4vityWall喜欢作者以教程方式解释问题，但不喜欢文章中的轻蔑语气。
• greatgib推荐使用acme.sh，认为它是一个简单且无复杂依赖的工具，非常容易使用和管理。
• sam_lowry_提到HTTP链接在现代应用中越来越不受支持，比如Whatsapp已经不允许打开HTTP链接，这使得从HTTP切换到HTTPS变得必要。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于ACME协议和JSON处理的复杂性。一部分人认为协议设计不合理，导致实现困难和安全隐患，而另一部分人则提供了实际解决方案或工具来简化这些问题。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同加密算法的优劣对比，特别是RSA与Ed25519的比较。

data.title: zeptoforth: A not-so-small Forth for ARM Cortex-M
data.author: thomascountz
data.article_summary: Zeptoforth 是一个针对 ARM Cortex-M 微控制器的原生代码 Forth 实现，包含实时操作系统（RTOS）及其他功能。它支持优先级调度的抢占式多任务和多处理，提供任务通知、信号量、锁（含优先级反转处理）、消息队列通道、双向同步回复通道等特性。其模块系统支持命名空间管理，易于定制构建以节省闪存空间。Zeptoforth 兼容 ANS Forth 和 Forth 2012 代码，但采用独特的异常处理和模块系统设计。API 文档可在 GitHub 获取，包含多核支持、GPIO 控制等丰富功能，特别适合资源充足的 Cortex-M 微控制器。

• Forth的被忽视可能与它的不常见和相对小众的使用群体有关，这使得其优点没有得到广泛传播和认可。

About zeptoforth
zeptoforth is an inlining native-code Forth implementation for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers which includes an RTOS and other batteries-added features. It is targeted at Cortex-M MCU's with larger flash sizes, due to the size of its included features and its heavy reliance upon inlining. It can compile to and execute from both flash and RAM; note that when compiling to flash flash is written immediately, no "save" operation is needed. It is highly modular, making use of a module system which enables easy namespace management so one does not have to worry about namespace pollution when developing code for it. Also, it is not difficult to put together custom builds that include just the subset of features one needs, e.g. to use less flash space.
zeptoforth is designed in particular as a priority-scheduled preemptive-multitasking and multiprocessing (on the Raspberry Pi Pico) Forth and provides a range of features to support this, including task notifications, semaphores, locks (with priority inversion resolution), queue channels, rendezvous channels, bidirectional channels (like rendezvous channels, but designed for sending a response to a given message), byte streams (like queue channels, but optimized for transferring arbitrary sequences of bytes), and interrupt service routine-safe channels (aka "simple channels" or "schannels" for short; like queue channels, but designed for being able to be used for sending messages to and from interrupt service routines). It also provides a purely round-robin "action scheduler" that enables lightweight asynchronous operation (without separate data and return stacks for each "action") with support for high-speed synchronous messaging between "actions" within a single task (as such it may only use a single core; also note that actions may only interact via messages with other actions within the same schedule). Using the action scheduler for multiple actions within a single task is highly recommended if maximum performance is needed, priority scheduling is not needed, blocking on anything other than message sending or receipt or fixed-length delays is not needed, multiprocessing is not needed, if separate data and return stacks are not needed, and/or if one has a large number of asynchronous elements (due to tasks being significantly heavier-weight than actions).
The philosophy of zeptoforth with regard to standardization is that ANS Forth and Forth 2012 code should be easy to port to it but it does not try hard too follow any particular standard. For instance, it supports and makes extensive use of quotations (via
[:
and
;]
), it has a somewhat different exception model (where execution tokens that print out an error message if executed, e.g. if uncaught, are used as exceptions rather than fixed numeric values; this is emphasized by the use of
try
rather than
catch
and
?raise
, along
triggers
and
averts
, rather than
throw
), it relies heavily upon a novel module system built on top of wordlists, it uses
[immediate]
and
[compile-only]
used
within
words rather than
immediate
and
compile-only
placed after words (
immediate
and
compile-only
do exist, but they are used for writing words for constructing other words), a heap allocator that takes a heap as an argument to
allocate
,
free
, and
resize
, rather than assuming a single global heap and which raises an exception on allocation failure, and it uses
not
rather than
invert
(as
invert
is an unfortunate ANS-ism).
API documentation is available
on GitHub
and in the docs directory on the build tarballs (which is the same as the html directory in git and in the source tarballs available on GitHub generated from that, which is built from the API documentation in Markdown format in the docs directory in git).
Included Features
zeptoforth includes the following features:
A priority-scheduled preemptive multitasker
Semaphores
Locks, with priority inversion handling
Message-oriented queue channels
Message-oriented rendezvous channels, aka "fchannels"
Message-oriented bidirectional synchronous reply channels, aka "rchannels"
Byte-oriented streams
Software alarms
Interrupt service handler-safe channels, aka "schannels"
Task notifications
Console redirection
Implicit compilation, i.e. automatically compiling temporary anonymous words from the REPL
Action scheduler support
Multicore support (on the RP2040 and the RP2350)
Double cell and S32.31 fixed-point numeric support
Lambda expressions
value
s and lexically scoped local variables
Closures
Object orientation
A disassembler
SysTick support
User-reconfigurable processor exception vector support
Interrupt-driven serial IO
Optional USB CDC console IO (on the RP2040 and the RP2350)
Rebooting via control-C on the console
GPIO support (including EXTI support on STM32 microcontrollers)

data.author: prawn
data.article_summary: 文章描述了作者在疫情期间逐渐对观鸟产生浓厚兴趣，并将其发展成一种全天候的爱好，称之为“birdpilled”（痴迷于鸟）。观鸟不仅仅是观察鸟类，更是对周围现实的全新认知和解读。作者详细描述了这种痴迷带来的体验：鸟儿无处不在，影响着日常生活，甚至带来冥想般的平静感。然而，电影中常出现错误的鸟类叫声，让作者感到困扰，尤其是《查理的天使》中的一幕，被认为是电影史上最错误的鸟类表现之一。作者深入调查这一错误，揭示了在耗资近1亿美元的电影中，为何没能准确呈现一只鸟，最终发现问题出在声音制作过程中的疏忽。文章改编自Slate播客《Decoder Ring》的一集。
